transcript:
00:00 Samantha Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we've got about an hour, appreciate the time. This is the RiverWatch implementation kickoff, want to make sure all stakeholders are on the same page. Monica, do you want to tee up RiverWatch goals?
00:14 Monica Reyes: Yeah hi all. We're trying to put model-driven alerts into our river level analytics pipeline, primary constraints are P95 latency under 500ms per request for the UI, and data residency — logs need to be retained per our compliance policy. We'll probably start with a small pilot, then ramp.
00:32 Dev Patel: Got it. Typical constraints. Just to call out, latency target's doable but depends on model choice and whether you're on Hosted or Dedicated. Dedicated gives more predictability for p95, hosted is faster to ship.
00:46 Liam O'Connor: Quick Q — what's the default data retention on hosted vs dedicated? Are logs held on your side?
00:52 Samantha Ortiz: Good question. We keep audit logs per account; retention depends on the plan. We'll send the SOC2 packet and the audit log retention table — but if you need bespoke retention we can talk enterprise options.
01:05 Priya Sharma: Security angle — we need KMS integration and SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. Also, we need to confirm encryption at rest and in transit, and whether customer-managed keys are supported in private deployments.
01:18 Dev Patel: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we have KMS integration with common providers and can enable envelope encryption. On Hosted we offer managed keys by default but can do HSM/KMS in some enterprise configs. I'll add details to the doc.
01:33 Ethan Cole: On networking — we plan to use a VPC peering model. Do you support direct peering, private link, or VPN? We need to know ports, CIDRs and the sequence for peering.
01:44 Hannah Li: We support VPC peering and private link-style connectivity depending on region. We'll provide a network diagram and the required CIDR ranges. Typical sequence: request peering, exchange routes, test connectivity, then we flip traffic.
01:58 Monica Reyes: For the pilot, we'll run a subset of inference traffic through Redwood and fail over to our fallback system if there are issues. What's the recommended canary percentage?
02:06 Dev Patel: We usually do 5–10% as a starting canary, measure throughput and tail latency. Canary duration depends on traffic —一天 （note: speaker attempted to say 'a day' but audio glitch) — usually 24–48 hours for stable signals. We'll also run a dedicated benchmark with your sample prompts to feed into kernel selection and batching configs.
02:28 Liam O'Connor: If we need lower latency at lower cost, do you recommend quantized models or batching tweaks?
02:33 Dev Patel: Yes. Quantization reduces memory and cost but can slightly affect quality. Batching and prefix/KV cache are big levers: if you have many short requests, batching may increase p50 but can hurt p95. We can tune continuous batching windows; also KV cache/prefix caching helps for repeated prompts like templated alerts.
02:56 Priya Sharma: Auditability — we need immutable logs for prompts and responses for compliance. How does Redwood surface those?
03:04 Samantha Ortiz: We provide audit logs via the console and syslog export options. For Private customers we can enable longer retention and export to your S3. We'll include sample log format in the package.
03:16 Ethan Cole: On the benchmarking — what do you need from us to run the Dedicated capacity test?
03:20 Dev Patel: Sample prompt set, token distribution (avg tokens in/out), concurrency targets, and a rough daily/peak QPS profile. Also any special sequence-length tail cases. If you share a 200–300 prompt sample that covers typical/edge cases we'd be good.
03:35 Monica Reyes: We'll compile those. Also FYI, we use proprietary tokenization for some pre- and post-processing, might add preproc time. We'll include notes.
03:45 Hannah Li: Great, include a sample preproc time per request so we can include it in end-to-end latency.
03:51 Samantha Ortiz: Timeline — we're proposing: share security docs this week, exchange network details early next week, benchmark week of 3/22, canary mid-April, and production after successful canary. Thoughts?
04:06 Liam O'Connor: That seems fine. Priya, any blockers from security?
04:10 Priya Sharma: Need to review SOC2 + encryption + KMS details. Also want to validate RBAC and SSO flow in a staging account before production.
04:19 Samantha Ortiz: We'll spin up a staging sandbox and a test SAML connection for you to validate. We'll also provide a runbook for common incidents and fallbacks.
04:29 Ethan Cole: A few practical items — can you share API key rotation policy and per-route quotas? We need to map to our rate limiters.
04:37 Dev Patel: Yes, rotation policy is in the security pack; per-route quotas and token-level throttles are configurable and we can set rate limits at customer and route levels.
04:46 Monica Reyes: Competitors note — we've also looked at Anthropic and a Vertex-managed endpoint for latency comparisons. One thing we liked about Redwood is the routing and automatic fallback model variants.
04:59 Dev Patel: Right. We can show a routing policy example — e.g., route to low-cost model when not in peak, fallback to smaller quantized variant if capacity constrained. That's part of Optimize recommendations.
05:12 Priya Sharma: For SSO, we use Okta with SAML2 and SCIM. We'll need a test IdP for staging.
05:18 Hannah Li: We'll provision a temporary test SP and guide you through the SAML metadata exchange.
05:23 Monica Reyes: Action items recap?
05:25 Samantha Ortiz: Sure — Samantha will send security/docs and the audit log sample; Dev will request sample prompts and propose benchmark dates; Hannah will share the runbook and canary template; Ethan will provide VPC CIDR and network contact. We'll schedule VPC network review with Priya.
05:42 Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Also please share rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our expected footprint — ballpark numbers are fine.
05:50 Dev Patel: We'll include a cost delta example in the follow-up, with assumptions on tokens, batching, and model family.
05:57 Priya Sharma: Minor transcription note — some of my audio was cut earlier during the canary question; please include the canary guidance in the doc.
06:04 Samantha Ortiz: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and propose slots for the benchmark.
06:10 Monica Reyes: Thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark.
06:14 [Meeting end]
